headline: Highest risk is medium: gpt-researcher can ingest local files and browse while opik has broad egress, creating plausible leakage and workflow-conflict paths; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content; opik exposes a REST API and broad egress, creating a plausible bridge if outputs are fed into it. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher consumes untrusted web or file content as instructions
IF opik ingests gpt-researcher outputs without provenance checks
IF both are connected through MCP or another shared channel
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported content
Add provenance tags to all gpt-researcher outputs
Require human review before opik consumes agent-generated text
Restrict MCP endpoints to allowlisted schemas
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, images, and secrets, while opik has broad network egress and a REST API. If they share a workspace or API path, sensitive research material could flow out through opik. No direct evidence shows the exact bridge, so uncertainty is resolved upward to medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or exported files
IF gpt-researcher processes documents containing secrets or sensitive research
IF opik forwards received content to a third-party service or remote backend
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Redact secrets before handing outputs to opik
Turn off upload of raw file contents where possible
Review REST payloads for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and use browsers; opik is not runnable and exposes only a REST API in this profile. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely, but shared mutable resources via external orchestration remain possible if the operator wires them together.
conditions: IF the operator gives both agents write access to the same directory or repo
IF an external orchestrator maps opik REST actions onto mutable resources
IF gpt-researcher is extended with write permissions not shown here
mitigations: Keep opik read-only in the shared workflow
Use separate directories for each agent
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
Serialize any file-producing steps
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and opik is an evaluation/observability tool that may consume those outputs. If opik treats the reports as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream judgments or actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF opik ingests gpt-researcher reports as ground truth
IF no verification step checks citations or source quality
IF downstream automation acts on the evaluated outputs
mitigations: Require source-link verification before evaluation
Sample-check citations against originals
Mark gpt-researcher output as untrusted by default
Add a human approval gate for downstream actions
requires-engineering: implement automated citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher explicitly handles local documents, citations, and multiple API keys, while opik’s profile shows no sensitive data classes or special residency obligations. The main compliance issue is a potential logging/retention mismatch if research data is sent into opik, but the profile does not show a direct residency conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data from gpt-researcher is forwarded into opik logs
IF opik retains evaluation traces longer than the source workflow
IF the operator requires deletion/export parity across both systems
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to opik
Minimize logged payloads
Set short retention on evaluation traces
Document deletion/export handling
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
